races.title: State Assembly, District 80
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: David A. Alvarez
cands.bio: Democrat representing California's 80th Assembly District since June 2022. Earlier served eight years on the San Diego City Council (District 8, 2010–2018). Owns Causa Consulting. Ran for San Diego mayor in 2014 and lost to Kevin Faulconer. Chaired the Assembly Legislative Audit Committee in 2023–24.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, Equality California and YIMBY Action.
In 2024 Ballotpedia lists an endorsement from the San Diego County Democratic Party.

cands.gaps: We found no documented actions or stated positions by Alvarez on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth limits, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. Ballotpedia's list of bills he sponsored was empty on the page we read. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026. His campaign site lists press-release headlines on housing, education and fuel bills, but we could not read the full releases, so we left them out. We found no controversies about him. We could not confirm the Ballotpedia entry showing a 2018 community college board race, so we left it out.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as San Diego, and his campaign site says he was born and raised in Barrio Logan, where he still lives with his family.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Eight years on the San Diego City Council (2010–2018), Assembly member since June 2022 (Budget Committee member, Legislative Audit Committee chair in 2023–24), and owner of Causa Consulting after about 15 years in government service.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service at both the city and state level, including work on the state budget, plus a consulting business. Committee roles were not counted toward the score.

cands.name: Alejandro Galicia
cands.bio: Republican candidate who ran for California State Assembly District 80 in 2026. He previously ran for San Diego County Board of Supervisors District 1 in 2024 and California State Senate District 18 in 2022. No offices held are documented.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists a 2026 endorsement from Reform California, along with voter guide recommendations from The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn and several Sway voting groups (April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Conservative California, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide).

cands.gaps: We could not find where he was born or raised, when he came to California, or his occupation and work history. He has never held public office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026, and we found no campaign site, questionnaire or interview stating his positions on data centers, property taxes, housing and land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. No documented controversies or foreign ties were found.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: No occupation or work history was found in the sources available. Ballotpedia lists only his unsuccessful campaigns for the State Senate (2022), County Board of Supervisors (2024) and State Assembly (2026).
qual.why: No career or office held could be verified, and a run for office alone is not scored.
